 Sharjah’s Al Qarayen 5 Park Shuts Temporarily For Al Dawahi Festival Preparations
 The neighbourhood park reopens on 10 December after Al Dawahi Festival preparations.
 by Deeplata Garde 
 Updated: November 16, 2026 2:19 PM 
 Share 
 Cover Image Courtesy: CanvaPro/Siarhei Nester from Pexels 
 If your weekend plans involved a stroll through Al Qarayen 5 Park in Sharjah, you’ll need to hold off for a few weeks. Sharjah Municipality has announced that the park will stay closed until 9 December 2026 and reopen to visitors on 10 December. 
 Why Is The Park Closing?  
 The closure is for preparations ahead of the annual Al Dawahi Festival. The neighbourhood park is the site being readied, which is why it is out of bounds until the work is done. 
 What Is The Al Dawahi Festival? 
 Organised by Sharjah Districts Affairs, Al Dawahi is a family-oriented festival that usually takes place during the school winter break. It brings together outdoor entertainment, cultural activities, food and attractions for children. Festival dates for this year had not been shared in the announcement we’ve seen, so keep an eye on official Sharjah channels for the schedule. 
 What Happened At Last Year’s Edition? 
 The previous edition gives a good idea of what to expect. The programme included: 
 Art exhibitions and interactive theatre 
 Educational and sports programmes 
 Training workshops and community initiatives 
 Daily television and radio broadcasts from the festival grounds 
 There were dedicated children’s areas and creative activities, plus space for local artisans. The festival also supported entrepreneurial projects developed by school and university students. 
 Also Read:  Sharjah Parks & Medical Fitness Centres Closed Amid Unstable Weather! 
 Why Winter Break Matters 
 Because the festival usually lands during the school winter break, families tend to plan around it well in advance. The park closing early is the municipality’s way of getting the grounds ready before the crowds arrive, so the festival can open on time and run smoothly once it begins. 
 Where Can Families Go In The Meantime? 
 With Al Qarayen 5 Park shut, residents of the surrounding area will need a different spot for their evening walks and weekend picnics. Sharjah has plenty of other public parks and green spaces, so check the municipality’s updates before you head out to avoid a wasted trip. 
 The Dates To Remember 
 Closed until: 9 December 2026 
 Reopens: 10 December 2026 
 Reason: preparations for the annual Al Dawahi Festival, organised by Sharjah Districts Affairs 
 Worth noting: the 10 December reopening is when the park returns to regular use, not necessarily when the festival begins. Until organisers confirm the dates, treat the two as separate. 
 If you live nearby, the closure is short and the dates are fixed, and the payoff is a festival the whole family can enjoy once the winter break starts. 
 Cover Image Courtesy: CanvaPro/Siarhei Nester from Pexels 
 FAQs
 What was in last year’s Al Dawahi Festival?
 The programme included art exhibitions, interactive theatre, educational and sports programmes, training workshops and community initiatives. It also featured children’s areas, local artisans, student-led entrepreneurial projects and daily TV and radio broadcasts from the grounds.
 What is the Al Dawahi Festival?
 It is a family-oriented festival organised by Sharjah Districts Affairs, typically held during the school winter break. It combines outdoor entertainment, cultural activities, food and attractions for children.
